result.title: DForkTree: Accelerating Speculative Decoding with Fork-Aware Block Diffusion Draft Trees
result.summary: Speculative decoding speeds up language models by letting a lightweight drafter propose several future tokens that the target model verifies in parallel. Block diffusion drafters such as DFlash draft a whole block in one forward pass, and DDTree builds a draft tree from their per-position distributions. Each of these distributions assumes that the drafter's own most likely continuation is correct. A tree, however, gains over a chain only on branches that leave this continuation, where the drafter's top-1 accuracy drops from 89% to 18% and its candidate lists miss the right token far more often. When re-run from the fork token, the same drafter is usually correct, so the errors come from the prefix that the distributions condition on rather than from what the drafter knows. We introduce DForkTree, a training-free method that re-anchors each branch on its own tokens. DForkTree adds n-gram statistics from the target model's own outputs to the drafter's scores as pointwise mutual information, weights them more after the fork, and builds the optimal tree under these scores exactly on the GPU. On Qwen3.5-4B and 9B, with all tree methods sharing one drafter, tree pipeline and verifier, DForkTree is the fastest tree method on every benchmark. It is up to 41.5% faster than DFlash and 15.1% faster than DDTree in the same setting, with average speedups of up to 4.75x over autoregressive decoding.

AI.brief_summary: 提出免训练方法 DForkTree：针对块扩散 drafter 构建的 draft tree，让每条分支重新锚定在自身 token 上，并把目标模型输出的 n-gram 统计以 PMI 形式加权到 drafter 分数（分叉后权重更高），在 GPU 上精确构造最优树以加速投机解码。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「树分支上的错误来自共享前缀条件而非 drafter 已知信息」的诊断，以及按分支重锚定与 PMI 重打分的候选树构造，可能可供核查并行 latent 假设的独立条件化、多分支打分与验证算力分配问题。
